results.context: adr: Move Widget Event Transport to EventBridge — domain eventing, repo svc-widgets; DRAFT, a proposal subject to change, not current platform direction
results.text: The draft proposes replacing the SQS standard queues used for event transport with an EventBridge event bus named `widgets-events` that uses rule-based routing. Each consumer would declare an EventBridge rule matching its event patterns, allowing new consumers to attach to the event bus without requiring changes to producers. | When: As of Thursday, August 20, 2026; this is a proposed future direction, not an implemented or accepted change. | Involving: Event producers would publish to the `widgets-events` EventBridge bus; each event consumer would declare its own matching rule; EventBridge would perform rule-based routing; and per-consumer SQS queues would receive routed events as targets. | The proposal is intended to remove the current consumer-onboarding friction caused by the SQS-per-event-class design. Its central operational benefit is that a new consumer can attach by adding its own matching rule rather than modifying producers or adding queue fan-out plumbing. This remains only a proposal because the document is explicitly a draft, has not been reviewed, and contains unresolved design questions.

results.text: The current SQS-per-event-class design consists of three SQS queues with one consumer group per queue. It is experiencing friction because adding a new consumer to an existing event class requires either adding queue fan-out plumbing or implementing filtering in the consumer. | When: As of Thursday, August 20, 2026; the text describes an ongoing current-state condition and does not specify when the friction began. | Involving: Event producers, existing and prospective event consumers, the three SQS queues, and the one-consumer-group-per-queue design. No individual people are named. | This friction is the motivation for considering a different transport topology: the current design makes onboarding an additional consumer to an existing event class operationally more complex by requiring producer-side or queue-side fan-out plumbing, or by shifting event-selection responsibility to consumer-side filtering.
